when_less: Inflation gets less attention than usual, because other subjects like AI and payments take more space. It is still one of the main subjects.

when_more: Interest rates are a hot subject. Borrowers and finance teams should follow the next ECB meetings closely.
when_less: Rates are discussed less than usual. Remember: rate talk mostly explains past decisions, so this says little about the next move.

when_more: Bond buying and loans to banks are discussed more. Watch for changes in how the ECB supports markets.
when_less: Bond buying is rarely discussed. The time of large bond purchases is behind us for now.

when_more: Bank rules and checks are in focus. Banks should expect closer supervision.
when_less: Bank supervision gets less space in speeches. This does not mean fewer checks on banks, only fewer headlines.

when_more: The ECB sees more risks to the financial system. Banks and investors should check how exposed they are to market stress.
when_less: Fewer warnings about financial crises than usual. The ECB sees the system as fairly stable.

when_more: Government debt worries the ECB more. Watch interest costs in countries with high debt.
when_less: Less talk about government debt than usual.

when_more: Closer EU ties and the euro's future are in focus. New EU market reforms or new euro countries may be coming.
when_less: Less talk about euro membership and EU integration than usual.

when_more: The ECB is watching growth and jobs closely. On the first page, this kind of worry about the economy often came before rate cuts.
when_less: Less focus on growth and jobs than usual.

when_more: New ways to pay and the digital euro are high on the agenda. Banks, payment companies and shops should plan how a digital euro would fit their systems and products.
when_less: Payments get less attention than usual.

when_more: Climate is back on the agenda. Banks and investors should expect more questions about climate risk in loans and investments, and companies more questions from lenders about their emissions.
when_less: Climate gets less attention than usual.

when_more: AI and new technology are now a top subject. Banks and fintechs should expect supervisors to ask how they use AI and how they control its risks.
when_less: Technology gets less attention than usual.

when_more: Trade, tariffs and tensions between countries worry the ECB. Exporters and companies with foreign suppliers should check how exposed they are to tariffs and currency swings.
when_less: Trade gets less attention than usual.

when_less: Fewer mentions of big outside shocks than usual.

when_more: The ECB is explaining itself and defending its role more than usual.
when_less: Less talk about the ECB's independence and communication than usual.
